title: Term and Ending Provisions by Plan, Workmanship Warranties
content:
Every Workmanship Warranties plan either runs for a fixed term in calendar months or runs, with no fixed term, for as long as the customer on file owns the vehicle. The table below states, for each plan, which of the two it is and the events that end or void it.

| Provision | Chip Repair Guarantee | Calibration Workmanship Warranty | Cosmetic Repair Workmanship Warranty | Glass Installation Lifetime Warranty | Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty | Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lasts as long as the customer on file owns the vehicle, without a fixed term | no | no | no | yes | yes | yes |
| Fixed term in calendar months from the issued date (0 means lifetime while owned) | 12 | 12 | 24 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Date the term counts from | issued date | issued date | issued date | issued date | issued date | issued date |
| Coverage ends when the customer on file no longer owns the vehicle | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Coverage is voided when the warrantied work is altered or re-repaired outside the network | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Coverage is voided when the vehicle is later declared a total loss | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| A rework starts a new term | no | no | no | no | no | no |

## Notes to the table

1. **Issued date.** The term counts from the issued date, which is the delivery or completion of the source work.
2. **Term months.** A plan with a figure above 0 has a fixed term of that many calendar months from the issued date: 12 months for the Chip Repair Guarantee and the Calibration Workmanship Warranty, 24 months for the Cosmetic Repair Workmanship Warranty. A figure of 0 means the plan is lifetime while owned: the Glass Installation Lifetime Warranty, the Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty and the Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty.
3. **Ending and voiding events.** Under every plan, coverage ends when the customer on file no longer owns the vehicle, and is voided when the warrantied work is altered or re-repaired outside the network or when the vehicle is later declared a total loss.
4. **Rework and term.** Under no plan does a rework start a new term.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Cosmetic Repair Workmanship Warranty issued on a hypothetical 10 March has a 24-month term counted from that issued date. A rework carried out under it during the term leaves the term where it was, because no plan restarts its term on a rework. A Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty, with a term figure of 0, has no fixed term at all and runs while the customer on file owns the vehicle.
